qt: to the Commission Cristina Guarda (Verts/ALE), Benedetta Scuderi (Verts/ALE), Leoluca Orlando (Verts/ALE), Ignazio Roberto Marino (Verts/ALE), Ilaria Salis (The Left), Alessandro Zan (S&D), Cecilia Strada (S&D), Mimmo Lucano (The Left), Sandro Ruotolo (S&D) Subject:

On 6 May 2024, a EUR 133 million contract for the operation of the Return Detention Centre (CPR) in Gjadër, Albania1, was awarded through a negotiated procedure without a call for tenders, following an expression of interest involving 30 entities. ActionAid reported the procedure to the National Anti-Corruption Authority (ANAC), pointing out its flaws, in particular, the failure to verify cross-border interest, which would have required an open and more transparent tender process2. The Commission wrote that it was monitoring the implementation of the protocol and its compatibility with Directive 2008/115/EC3. Once again, the problems caused by externalising migration policies need to be highlighted. In view of the above: 1.
Does the contract award procedure conform with Directive 2014/24/EU on public procurement?
What are the results of the monitoring of the implementation of the protocol?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (9.3.2026) The Commission notes that national courts are primarily responsible to assess whether, according to the relevant legal and factual circumstances of each individual case, contracting authorities and contracting entities respected their obligations under EU law. The Commission remains in contact with the Italian authorities on migration management. Concerning the bilateral Italy-Albania protocol, the Commission kindly refers the Honourable Members to the replies provided to parliamentary questions P-002206/2024, E-001425/2025 and E-001648/2025.
